instrument: the SECURED revision, measured — whole-population scss row, css re-check, and whether the new mechanism is reachable at all
revision: HEAD after the secured commits (scss analyzer +86, the DeclarationKind member, .scss added to PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS)

gates.exit: 0 (the gate parses incoming-gate's non-zero exit by design)

scssStandardArm.verdict: IDENTICAL to the pre-secured row — every column (exports, references, imports, extends, calls, overrides, uses, contains, TOTAL) is UNCHANGED.
scssStandardArm.whyItMeansLittle: AND IT EXERCISES NONE OF THE NEW CODE, which the Lead asked me to say if it were true: `residual-gate --lane scss` invokes `incoming-gate.ts scss scss 0` WITH NO `--index` FLAG, so `useIndex` is false and `parseFile` is called without a `projectIndex`. The new `resolveModuleImports` gates on `ctx.projectIndex`, so it never runs in this row.

scssIndexedArm.whatItActuallyIs: AN EMPTY-INDEX ARM, NOT PRODUCTION'S. The gate printed `project index: USED — 0 repo index(es) (0 built, 0 from cache, 0 damaged) over 0 file(s)`. So it hands the analyzer a `projectIndex` KEY with nothing in it.
scssIndexedArm.reading: resolved -930 · ambiguity +1,367 · extOK 6,841 -> 0. The mere PRESENCE of a `projectIndex` key changes the lane materially even when the index is empty — which is exactly the state a broken build path would produce.

cssRow.verdict: 0 of 6 columns differ from the pre-secured row — references, imports, uses, contains, overrides, TOTAL all identical. The verified neighbour is unmoved.

isTheMechanismReachable.answer: NO — not with the spec it needs, in three places, and this is the finding that matters more than the row:
isTheMechanismReachable.1_specUnexported: `src/ast/project-index.ts:470` declares `const SCSS_DECLARATION_SPEC: DeclarationSpec = {…}` WITHOUT `export`, while `SOLIDITY_`, `PYTHON_`, `DART_` and `FSHARP_DECLARATION_SPEC` are all exported.
isTheMechanismReachable.2_runFixturesReadsItAnyway: `script/m14/run-fixtures.ts:648` reads `mod.SCSS_DECLARATION_SPEC` (via an `any` module handle), which is therefore **undefined**, and `buildProjectIndexFromDisk(..., spec: DeclarationSpec = SOLIDITY_DECLARATION_SPEC)` falls back to **SOLIDITY'S spec** for SCSS files. So `run-fixtures` passing does not validate the new mechanism.
isTheMechanismReachable.3_productionUsesTheWrongSpecToo: `src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts` maps wasm per language INCLUDING `scss: tree-sitter-scss.wasm` (so it will try), but `specByLang` carries only `solidity`, `fsharp`, `protobuf` → `specByLang["scss"] ?? mod.SOLIDITY_DECLARATION_SPEC` indexes SCSS declarations with the SOLIDITY spec. `.scss` was added to `PROJECT_INDEX_EXTENSIONS` without its spec being reachable.
isTheMechanismReachable.4_gateCannotBuildOne: the gate's own builder reports 0 indexes built for scss, so the arm that would measure the mechanism cannot be produced by the gate as it stands.

consequenceForTheVerdicts: scss's row is unchanged on the arm anyone can reproduce, and css's row is unmoved — so both verdicts stand on the secured revision as far as those rows go. But the new mechanism is NOT proven by them: it is unreachable with the right spec (unexported, unmapped, and built with Solidity's spec in both callers), and the only arm that hands the analyzer an index (empty) moves three columns DOWN.
